Vs.

full_judgment:
Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.- This rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Bakerganj and opposite party informant Khorshed Ali Bepari to show cause why the impugned orders passed on 24-3-77' and 27-7-77 in Special Tribunal Case No. 68 of 1977 should not be set aside and the proceedings against the accused petitioners should not be quashed. The facts of the case, briefly stated are as follows: On 2-2-76 informant Khorshed Ali Bepari lodged an F.I.R. at P.S. Babuganj, District Bakerganj alleging that on 31-1-76 between 20.00 hrs and 23.00 hrs. accused petitioners Nuru Bepari, ZamZam Bepari, Abdul Khaleque Fakir and Habibur Rahman Howlader and 16/17 others being armed with guns, Ram Dao, Leja etc. raided the house of informant's father-in-law Abdul Kader Bepari, that he said dacoits had torch lights with them, that they looted away paddy worth Tk. 4,500/00, that during the occurrence Nazem Ali Akand, son of late Amjad Ali Akand was killed by the dacoits and that the dacoits escaped on the approach of the villagers. After investigation police submitted final report on 29-8-76 (Annexure-A) On 29-8-76 Sub-Inspector Molla Sahidul Islam of Babuganj Police station started counter case against informant Khorshed Ali Bepari and 9 others by lodging an F.I.R. In the said counter case the police submitted charge-sheet against the informant opposite party Khorshed Ali Bepari and II others on 23-9-76 under sections 364/302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 2. On the basis of the F.I.R. lodged by informant opposite party Khorshed Ali Bepari on 2-2-76 G.R. case No. 65 of 1976 was started in the Court of Sub-divisional Magistrate, Sadar (S) Bakerganj. After the final report was submitted by the police, informant opposite party Khorshed Ali Bepari filed a naraji petition and the learned Sub divisional Magistrate after a judicial enquiry forwarded the case to the Special Tribunal No. 1, Bakerganj for taking cognizance under section 396 of the Penal Code. 

 3. On 24-3-77 the learned Special Tribunal No. 1 passed the following order in the said case which was numbered Special Tribunal Case No. 66 of 1977. 

 "The case is put up today for hearing and orders. 

 Heard learned Advocate for the aced and also the learned P.P The I.O has collected materials in this case but he has opined that those materials were not reliable. He has therefore usurped the power of the Court and has given a positive opinion on the efficacy of the evidence. The 1.0 has therefore gone far beyond his jurisdiction. In this case there are incriminating materials against the aced. The final report is a police report within the meaning of section 173 Cr.P.C. and so it is within the competence of the Tribunal to take cognizance on the basis of that report. 

 The four accused persons filed a petition before the learned Special Tribunal No. 3 who on 27-7-77 passed the following order in the said Special Tribunal Case No. 68 of 1977 

 4. Mr. Abu Backkar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioners argues that the impugned orders passed on 24.3.77 and 27.7.77 taking cognizance of the case under section 27 of the Special Powers Act arc bad in law inasmuch as there is no charge sheet submitted by the Police against the accused petitioners as contemplated under section 27 of the Special Powers Act. He argues that as final report was submitted against the accused persons by the police, the impugned order taking cognizance of the offence under section 396 of the Penal Code read with the Special Powers Act by the special Tribunal is not sustainable in law and therefore, the proceeding against the accused petitioners before the Special Tribunal should be quashed. In support of his argument he referred to the decision in the case of Dost Mohammad Vs. State, 29 DLR 122 and the decision of the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 107 of 1977. 

 5. Mr. Md. Anwar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the State, referred to the decisions in the cases of Md. Kalu Bhuiyan Vs. Special Tribunal No. II, Comilla and another, 30 DLR 124 and Falak Sher Vs. State 19 DLR (SC) 426 and argues that the charge-sheet and the final report are both included in the expression "a report in writing made by Police Officer" referred to in section 27(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 and that the Special Tribunal is competent to take cognizance of an offence under section 396 of the Penal Code read with the Special Powers Act against the accused petitioners on the basis of such report in writing submitted by the Police. He also referred to the decision in the case of Salimuddin Ahmed Vs. State 28 DLR 187 wherein it was held that in view of the provision of clause of section 30 of the Special Powers Act this Court has no jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash the proceeding pending before a Special Tribunal constituted under the Special Powers Act. 

 6. The decision in the case of Dost Mohammad vs. The State, 29 DLR 122 (Badrul Haider Chowdhury and Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury J. does not apply in this case as the complaint in the said case did not dis-close any offence coming within the mischief of the Special Powers Act and the Court held that the cognizance was taken by the learned Special Tribunal under section 190(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and not under Section 27 of the Special Powers Act upon a police report: Further in that case it was not brought to the notice of the Court that section 30(1) of the Special Powers Act provides that "save as aforesaid there shall be no appeal from any order, judgment or sentence of a Special Tribunal and no Court shall have authority to revise such' order, judgment or sentence." 

 7. The decision of their Lordships of the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 107 of 1977 also has no application in this case. It is to be noted that the said decision of the Appellate Division is in exercise of power under Article 102 of the Constitution. In the said decision their Lordships of the Appellate Division set aside the order of the learned Sessions Judge because the learned Sessions Judge while exercising his revisional power under the Code of the Criminal Procedure took cognizance of the case under the Special Power Act. Their Lordships observed: "Instance are not lacking when the same court or person has been invested with dual and distinct capacities. In this case, the Sessions Judge of a district, who has also been empowered to exercise the powers of Special Tribunal, constituted under the Special Powers Act, was exercising the revisional powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure. But the Act has provided the circumstances in which the Sessions Judge can exercise his powers under the Act: There is no provision in the Act itself nor can it be implied from the provisions thereof that the legislature intended that the powers conferred under the Act and those under the Code of Criminal Procedure could be exercised in either capacity according to necessity, just because the records were before him." 

 8. In the present case, the F.I.R. discloses a prima facie offence under section 396 of the Penal Code coming within the mischief of the Special Powers Act. The Police investigated into the case and submitted a report in writing which has been sent by the learned Divisional Magistrate to the Special Tribunal. The fact that in the meanwhile there was a judicial enquiry in the case is superfluous and irrelevant. The learned Special Tribunal has made it clear that he has taken cognizance of the offence against the accused petitioners under section 27(1) of the Special Powers Act on receipt of the report in writing submitted by the police. In the case of Md. Kalu Bhuiyan Vs. Special Tribunal No. II Comilla and another, 30 DLR 124 it was held by the Division Bench presided over by Ruhul Islam, J. that the conclusion of the Police in the report submitted under section 27(1) of the Special Powers Act is not binding upon the Special Tribunal. In the said case it was observed: "He (Special Tribunal) is free to decide in a case where he does not puree with the conclusion of the Investigating Officer and he is satisfied from the facts of the case as appearing from the police report and other connected papers, that the offender should be placed on trial for determining as to whether he is guilty or not, is competent to take cognizance of the offence and proceed with the trial. Such action will be under section 27(1) of the Special Powers Act corresponding to an action under section 190(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In such a case the Special Judge takes cognizance independent of sec. 190(I)(b) and on the basis of the power as contained in section 27(1) of the Special Powers Act." We are in respectful agreement with the said view. As section 27(1) of  Spectral Powers Act corresponds to section 190(I)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure this view also finds support in the decision in the case of Falak Sher Vs. State, 19 DLR (SC) 426. Thus in the instant case the learned Special Tribunal committed no illegality in taking cognizance of the case against the accused petitioner after the submission of the report in writing by a competent Police Officer. 

 9. The question of utmost importance in this Case is whether this Court has jurisdiction to quash the proceeding before the Special Tribunal or to set aside the order passed by the Special Tribunal. As already stated, Clause (1) of section 30 inter alia, provides that "save as aforesaid there shall be no appeal from any order, Judgment or sentence of a Special Tribunal and no Court shall have authority to revise such order, judgment or sentence." A plain reading of the said provision will show that after stating in section 29 of the Act that except where it is not inconsistent with the Act the provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure will apply to the proceedings of the Special Tribunal, section 30(1) of the Act has taken away the jurisdiction of this set aside any order passed by the Special Tribunal or to quash the proceeding pending before the Special Tribunal in exercise of power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, The application by the accused petitioner for quashing the proceeding in question by this Court is thus also not maintainable. 

 The rule is accordingly discharged. The order staying proceedings of the case is vacated. A.T.M. Masud, J.--I agree.
